title: introduce-cost-bento-tenant-budget-nudger-and-quant-curation-pipeline
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Tenant ops and platform SREs asked for a light-weight 'budget nudge' mechanism that can proactively recommend budget-safe defaults and apply soft constraints when unit-econ signals indicate drift. This PR adds a modular pipeline (Cost Bento) that: 1) consumes unit-econ telemetry and tenant budget manifests, 2) synthesizes per-tenant budget nudges and safe quantization tiers, and 3) exposes a dry-run and a shadow-run capability so account teams can validate changes before rollout.

What's included (high level): - cost-bento service (new microservice under infra/cost_bento) implementing the core nudger and quant-curation logic - budget-manifests-as-code schema (yaml) and a small CLI to validate and dry-run manifests (tools/cost-bento-cli) - quant-curation rules engine: a small deterministic rule runner that maps workload signatures to quant tiers and safety fallbacks (runtime/quant/curator) - telemetry gating and simulation: an offline simulator to estimate token-cost delta and latency impact for suggested changes (tools/simulate-cost-delta) - operator UI hooks: simple REST endpoints to preview, accept, or reject suggested nudges, and a webhook for automated apply-by-policy (api/cost-bento) - integration tests and unit-econ fixtures (tests/cost_bento)

Design notes: - The nudger intentionally produces "soft" suggestions (nudge, not hard-enforce) flagged with confidence levels. Suggestions with low confidence are marked for human review. - Quant-curation uses a tiered approach: safe, lite, compact. Fallbacks are explicit and annotated with expected token savings and worst-case latency regression. - Budget manifests allow TTL for suggestions and a per-tenant maximum allowed quality delta (to prevent silent regressions). - Simulation runs against a 7-day rolling sample of traces (sanitized). The simulator outputs a small report used by the CLI and UI.

Checklist: - [x] Service scaffolding and API - [x] Rules engine with unit tests - [x] CLI validate/dry-run - [x] Offline simulator and sample fixtures - [x] Telemetry gating and confidence annotations - [x] Integration tests in CI - [x] Small docs: README, operator guide

Testing & CI: CI runs unit tests for the rules engine, e2e integration with a lightweight docker-compose setup, and static analysis on manifests. A temporary flaky test was quarantined and tracked in ENG-4129. All checks green on final run (unit, integration, linters).

Rollout plan: Merge to main behind feature-flag (feature.cost_bento.enabled = false). Enable in staging and run 48h shadow-mode against the staging tenant weight. After operator validation, flip to opt-in by default for tenants with budget manifests.

Release notes (for changelog): Introduce Cost Bento: tenant budget nudger and quant-curation pipeline. Adds CLI for manifest validation and dry-run simulation. Backwards-compatible; off by default behind feature flag.

review_thread: Ari Patel: Nice direction — can you explain how confidence is computed? The PR mentions confidence but no metric list.

Maya Chen: Confidence is a composite score: sample coverage (fraction of traces matched), model-stability (historical variance of token counts), and sim-estimate margin. I added a doc section enumerating the components and thresholds.
Daniel Groff: Two nit picks on API shape: prefer POST /suggestions/dryrun and include tenant_id in header rather than body for forwarding. Also add rate limiting to the endpoint.
Maya Chen: Updated routes.py to accept tenant_id via X-Tenant-ID header and added token-bucket limiter at 100r/m. Adjusted CLI examples.
Sofia Márquez: Telemetry sampling used in simulator — are sanitized traces PII-free? Please confirm and add a scrubber utility.
Maya Chen: Added scrubber util and explicit sanitizer in sim.py; included notes in operator guide about dataset retention and scrubbing policy.
Ari Patel: Integration tests look flaky on CI due to docker-compose timing. Add retry/backoff in the test harness.
Maya Chen: Added exponential backoff helper and increased default wait to 60s in e2e. Re-ran CI; green.
merge_summary: Merged by squash via web UI after approvals from Ari Patel and Daniel Groff. Feature gated; config flag added to config/feature_flags.toml.
notes_for_ops: Feature is disabled by default. To enable: set feature.cost_bento.enabled=true in the staging cluster config, create tenant budget manifests under /etc/redwood/budgets/<tenant>.yml and run tools/cost-bento-cli validate <path>. When ready, enable shadow mode and monitor cost.delta and quality.regression dashboards.
release_notes: Add Cost Bento service: tenant budget nudger with quant-curation and simulation CLI. Off by default behind feature flag. Non-breaking. See docs/cost-bento for operator steps.
